problem:
![](images/b7/b70d2d8824cfbebbff2807239cf9b98796b43e8cb0f74e7e43ae25eb28b79086.png)

Consider the vector field $F$ shown above, and let $C$ be the path along the segment $AB^(―)$ traversed from $A$ to $B$. Which of the following statements are true?

1. $$
\displaystyle \int_{C}F \cdot dr > 0
$$
2. $$
\displaystyle \int_{C}F \cdot dr < 0
$$
3. $$
\displaystyle \int_{-C}F \cdot dr > 0
$$
worked_solution:
Along the segment from $A$ to $B$, both the field arrows and the direction of traversal point right. Their dot product is positive, so

$$
\int_C F\cdot dr>0.
$$

Reversing the path changes the sign of a vector line integral:

$$
\int_{-C}F\cdot dr=-\int_C F\cdot dr<0.
$$

Therefore statement I only is true.
